title: SpaceX Disappoints, AI's Free Cash Flow Shrinks, Meta Struggles | The Weekly Wrap
summary: Eisman explains how correlated long and short AI exposures amplify leverage risk, then focuses on shrinking hyperscaler cash flow and still-open private-credit refinancing risk. He sees more differentiation among software companies, favors long-term AI infrastructure holdings, and questions SpaceX valuation and its mixed business model.
assessment: Full transcript reviewed. Empirical claims without inspected primary outcome evidence remain unresolved; guest claims are separate from Eisman attribution. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman hosts the episode; guest turns are inferred from introductions and conversational context.
framework_points: Evaluate gross leverage together with common thesis exposure on both sides of a hedge fund.
Separate real franchises from indiscriminate sector repricing.
A high earnings multiple makes quarterly expectation gaps difficult to trade.
Profit growth does not eliminate capital-intensity and cash-flow risks.
tools_and_charts: Hypothetical $100m long/$100m short portfolio backed by $50m equity
transcript_cautions: The Goldman/FICO pairing and automobile/carriage pairing are hypothetical illustrations, not disclosed actual fund positions.
Amazon's June-ended cash-flow period is called its fiscal year; verify whether trailing twelve months was intended.
SpaceX's stated $1.6tn market cap divided by $31.2bn annualized revenue is about 51.3, not 54.

claims.claim: AI capital spending is compressing cash generation at Microsoft, Amazon and Meta despite strong revenue growth.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare the stated proposition with Microsoft fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter earnings call; Meta second-quarter 2026 results. Preserve the metric, reporting period and conditions; agreement on direction alone does not prove a causal explanation.
claims.reason: Microsoft, Amazon and Meta filings verify substantial capital expenditure and cash-flow pressure. Amazon trailing-year FCF was negative $7.604bn. Meta expense growth also contains legal and severance charges, so the numerical cash-flow pattern alone does not establish an exclusively AI cause.

evidence.title: Microsoft fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter earnings call
evidence.finding: Azure grew 43%, revenue 18%; adjusted EPS $4.74 grew 23%, not 30%; operating cash $55.4bn less cash PP&E $35.8bn gives FCF $19.6bn. RPO $678bn; non-OpenAI RPO growth 25%.

evidence.title: Meta second-quarter 2026 results
evidence.finding: Revenue $60.801bn up 28%; expenses $42.026bn up 55%, including $2.40bn legal and $1.18bn severance; EPS $6.18 down 13%; FCF $784m; annual capex guide $130-145bn.

evidence.title: Amazon Q2 2026 Form 10-Q
evidence.finding: Trailing-year operating cash $161.403bn less net PP&E purchases $169.007bn gives free cash flow negative $7.604bn.
